name: Mullaivananathar Temple (Garbharakshambigai)
significance: Shiva shrine on the Kaveri attributed to the Early Chola king Killivalavan, counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams hymned by Tirugnanasambandar. Its goddess Garbharakshambigai draws devotees seeking safe pregnancy and childbirth.
story: The goddess is believed to have received her initiation at this shrine.

name: Palaivananathar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the 7th-century Tevaram, at Papanasam in the Kaveri delta. The Chola-founded complex was rebuilt in masonry under 16th-century Vijayanagar rule, with a granary added by Raghunatha Nayak, and carries inscriptions of Kulothunga Chola I and III.
story: Shiva is said to have absolved the sins of Vishnu, Brahma, Rama and Sita here, earning the name Papanasanathar, the destroyer of sins.

name: Kalyanasundaresar Temple
significance: A 9th-century Chola perunkoil on an elevated platform near Kumbakonam, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram as a Paadal Petra Sthalam. Inscriptions of Uttama Chola and Raja Raja Chola survive, and Vijayanagar dynasties later expanded it.
story: Sage Agastya is said to have witnessed the wedding of Shiva and Parvati at this spot and installed a lingam here.

name: Pasupatheeswarar Temple
significance: An elevated maadakoil counted among the 70 temples attributed to the 7th-century king Kochengat Chola, with its present masonry from the 9th-century Cholas and Nayak-era expansions. A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by Sambandar, noted for its rare set of five Bhairava images.
story: The celestial cow Kamadhenu is said to have worshipped Shiva here to be freed from sage Vasishtha's curse.

name: Sakthivanesvara Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Patteeswaram whose lingam bears the mark of Parvati's embrace, glorified in the Tevaram hymns. Devotees pray here to be blessed with the life partner of their choice.
story: Parvati is said to have done penance here and embraced Shiva when he appeared as a column of fire, giving the place its name Sakthimutram.

name: Thenupuriswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Kumbakonam revered in the 7th-century Tevaram, founded under the Cholas and given its present masonry form by the 16th-century Nayaks.
story: When Sambandar arrived in scorching heat, Shiva sent attendants with a pearl canopy and ordered Nandi to move aside so the saint could see the sanctum from outside.

name: Pazhayarai Vadathali Temple
significance: The northern shrine of Pazhayarai, a capital region of the Chola empire near Kumbakonam, with inscriptions from the 8th-9th centuries and a Later Chola gopuram. It is revered as a Paadal Petra Sthalam in the Tevaram.
story: The moon god is said to have worshipped Shiva at this spot, prompting the lord's appearance.

name: Kabartheeswarar Temple
significance: One of the largest temple complexes in Tamil Nadu, with a seven-tiered gopuram and three precincts, built up from Chola-era masonry with Thanjavur Nayak expansions. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified in the 7th-century Tevaram.
story: The sage Herandar is said to have travelled underground to bring the Kaveri to earth, making the river swirl around this place - hence the name Thiruvalanchuzhi.

name: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple
significance: The principal Shiva temple of Kumbakonam, founded by the 9th-century Cholas and enlarged by the Thanjavur Nayaks, spread over three concentric compounds with four gopurams. A Paadal Petra Sthalam and one of the twelve temples tied to the Mahamaham festival held every twelve years.
story: The town's name is traced to Brahma's pot of creation-seeds, which Shiva's arrow displaced so that nectar fell at this spot.

name: Nageswaraswamy Temple (Kudanthai Keezhkottam)
deity: Shiva (Nageswarar, lord of the serpent king), consort Periyanayagi
significance: Reckoned among the earliest of all Chola temples, raised in the 9th century under Aditya Chola in Kumbakonam. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam revered by the Nayanars in the Tevaram.
story: During Rajendra Chola's Ganges expedition the army is said to have brought back a beautiful Vinayagar image, installed here as Gangai Vinayagar.

name: Kasi Viswanathar Temple (Kudanthai Karonam)
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Kumbakonam revered in the 7th-century Tevaram, rebuilt in the 16th century during the Nayak period. It is one of the twelve Shiva temples connected with the Mahamaham festival.
story: Rama and Lakshmana are said to have worshipped Shiva here while searching for Sita, obtaining Rudramsam to fight Ravana.

name: Naganathar Temple
significance: A Chola-built Paadal Petra Sthalam near Kumbakonam, famous as the Rahu shrine among the Navagraha temples of the Kaveri delta. The presiding Naganathar is revered in the 7th-century Tevaram.
story: Serpent deities led by Adishesha are said to have done penance here and won Shiva's grace, giving the lord his name Naganathar.

name: Mahalingeswarar Temple
significance: One of the great Shaiva temples of the Kaveri delta, its oldest masonry from the 9th-century Cholas with four gopurams and three precincts expanded under the Thanjavur Nayaks. A Paadal Petra Sthalam counted among the foremost shrines of Saivism.
story: A Chola prince pursued by a Brahmin's vengeful spirit is said to have entered the temple, prayed to Shiva, and escaped through another gate - a circuit worshippers still repeat.

name: Abathsahayeswarar Temple (Then Kurangaduthurai)
significance: The Then Kurangaduthurai shrine at Aduthurai, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the Tevaram, founded by the Cholas and rebuilt in masonry during the 16th-century Nayak period.
story: Sugriva, fleeing his brother Vali, is said to have prayed to Shiva here and been rescued when the lord turned him into a swan.

name: Umamaheswarar Temple
significance: The Tirunallam shrine of the Tevaram, rebuilt in the 10th century by the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi over an earlier foundation. It is noted for the paintings of its front mandapa and the miniature sculptures outside the sanctum.

name: Kokileswarar Temple
significance: A Kaveri-bank Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified by the Tamil Saivite saints in the early medieval Tevaram poems.
story: A devotee named Chandan, cursed by Indra to be reborn as a nightingale (kokila), is said to have regained human form by meditating on Shiva here.

name: Masilamaniswara Temple
significance: A 9th-century Chola temple at Thiruvaduthurai on the Kaveri, expanded by later Chola rulers and rich in inscriptions from the reigns of Parantaka I and Rajaraja I. It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams of the Tevaram canon.
story: The saint Tirumular is said to have entered the body of the dead herdsman Moolan here to console his grieving cattle, and remained in that form for good.

name: Ukthavedeeswarar Temple
significance: A Kaveri-bank shrine celebrated by Sambandar in the Tevaram, held in tradition to be the venue of Shiva's wedding to Parvati.
story: After the wedding held here, Shiva is said to have left his sandals behind before setting out for Mount Kailash.

name: Vedapureeswarar Temple
significance: A Kaveri-bank Paadal Petra Sthalam at Therazhundur glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram, bearing Imperial Chola inscriptions dated to the reign of Kulottunga Chola I.

name: Mayuranathaswami Temple
significance: The great temple of Mayiladuthurai, attested in the 7th-century hymns of Appar and Sambandar and renovated by queen Sembiyan Mahadevi in the 10th century. It ranks among the six Kaveri shrines held equal to Kashi Vishwanath of Varanasi.
story: Parvati, cursed to become a peahen, is said to have worshipped Shiva here and regained her form as Abhayambika - giving the town its name, Mayiladuthurai.

name: Uchiravaneswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Uchira Vaneswarar), consort Veyuru Tholi Ammai
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified in the medieval Tevaram hymns of Tirugnanasambandar at Vilanagar near Mayiladuthurai.

name: Veerateswarar Temple
significance: One of the eight Ashta Veeratta sthalams marking Shiva's heroic deeds - here the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice - built by the 9th-century Cholas and expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon.
story: Shiva is said to have destroyed Daksha for insulting Dakshayani at his sacrifice, then restored him to life with a goat's head.

name: Swarnapureeswarar Temple
significance: The Tiruchemponpalli shrine on the Kaveri, a Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified by both Sambandar and Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram.

name: Natrunaiyappar Temple
deity: Shiva (Natrunaiyappar), consorts Malaiyaan Madanthai and Parvatha Putthiri
significance: The Tirunanipalli shrine of the Tevaram, built by Parantaka Chola I in the 10th century, whose unusually large sanctum is said to have once admitted elephants for worship.
story: Shiva is believed to have granted wedding darshan here to Vinayaka and the sage Agastya.

name: Valampurinathar Temple
significance: The Tiruvalampuram shrine near the Kaveri's mouth, raised in the medieval Chola period and revered as a Paadal Petra Sthalam in the 7th-century Tevaram hymns.

name: Sankaranyeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva (Sankaranyeswarar, as Somaskandar), consort Soundara Nayaki
significance: A conch-shaped shrine at Thalaichangadu attributed to the Early Chola king Kochengannan and renovated over later centuries, praised by Sambandar in the Tevaram.
story: Vishnu is believed to have worshipped Shiva at this place.

name: Thanthondreeswarar Temple
significance: The self-manifested Shiva shrine of Aakkur, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by the Nayanars in the early medieval Tevaram.
story: An ailing Chola king fed a thousand guests for 48 days; Shiva is said to have come as the thousandth and cured him, after which the temple rose here.

name: Amritaghateswarar-Abirami Temple
significance: The celebrated shrine where Shiva is held to have conquered death itself, saving the boy-sage Markandeya from Yama - hence his name Kala-samhara. A 9th-century Chola foundation expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks, and a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram.
story: When Yama came for the sixteen-year-old devotee Markandeya, Shiva burst from the lingam and subdued death, granting the boy eternal youth.

name: Brahmapureeswarar Temple
significance: The Tirukkadavur Mayanam shrine beside Thirukkadaiyur, one of the five sacred Mayana (cremation-ground) kshetras where Shiva is held to have burnt Brahma to ashes. A Paadal Petra Sthalam with Chola-era idols and Vijayanagar-period inscriptions.
story: At the end of every eon Shiva burns Brahma to ashes, and the celestials pleaded here for Brahma's restoration so creation could continue.

name: Sundareshwarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in the Karaikal district of Puducherry, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Parvatheeswarar Temple
significance: The Tiruttelicheri shrine, in the village now called Koilpathu on the periphery of Karaikal, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams sung by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram.

name: Yazhmoorinathar Temple
significance: The Dharmapuram shrine near Karaikal in the Union Territory of Puducherry, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram; its deity's name recalls the bending of the yazh, the ancient Tamil lute.

name: Dharbaranyeswarar Temple (Thirunallar Saniswaran Temple)
deity: Shiva (Dharbaranyeswarar), consort Praneswari Amman; shrine of Shani (Saturn)
significance: The most famous Shani shrine among the nine Navagraha temples of the Kaveri delta, where Saturn's image stands within a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Shiva. The present masonry is 9th-century Chola work with Vijayanagar-era expansions.
story: When a corrupt headman threatened a shepherd who supplied milk for the lord's ablutions, Shiva is said to have intervened with his trident to stop the king's punishment.

name: Iravatheeswarar Temple
significance: A roughly thousand-year-old Medieval Chola shrine at Tirukkottaru, whose Tevaram praise by Sambandar is inscribed within the sanctum itself.
story: Indra's elephant Airavata, cursed by the sage Durvasa, is said to have worshipped here among the holy places that freed him after a hundred years.

name: Mahakalanathar Temple
significance: The Ambar Maakaalam shrine, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Meganathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram, renowned for its shrine of Lalithambika: tradition holds that the Lalita Sahasranama was composed here and taught to Agastya by Hayagriva.
story: Garuda and Aruna, mounts of Vishnu and Surya, are said to have been born here to Vinata and Kadru after the sisters worshipped Shiva.

name: Sakalabhuvaneswarar Temple (Ilamkovil)
significance: The Ilamkovil or younger shrine within the Tirumeeyachur temple precinct, counted separately among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and glorified by Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram.

name: Muktheeswarar Temple
significance: The Thilataipati (Thilatharpanapuri) shrine at Sethalapathy in Tiruvarur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams celebrated by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram.

name: Paampuranathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon where devotees especially seek relief from Rahu-Ketu and serpent doshas, and pray against childlessness.

name: Sukshmapureeswarar Temple
significance: The Sirukudi shrine in Tiruvarur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Veezhinathar Temple
significance: The 61st Paadal Petra shrine of Chola Nadu south of the Kaveri, in Kudavasal taluk of Tiruvarur district, where Parvati reborn as Katyayani is held to have wed Shiva.
story: The saint Mizhalai Kurumbar offered vila fruit to Shiva each day and was rewarded with the lord's darshan.

name: Agnipureeswarar Temple
significance: The Tiruvanniyur shrine in the Kaveri delta, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, glorified by the Nayanar Tirunavukkarasar in the Tevaram.

name: Sarguneswarar Temple
significance: The Karuvili Kottittai shrine of the Tevaram canon in Tiruvarur district, where worship is believed to grant salvation and release from rebirth.

name: Sivanandeswarar Temple
significance: The Penu Perunturai shrine near Kumbakonam, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the early medieval Tevaram poems.

name: Siddhanatheswarar Temple
significance: The Naraiyur shrine in present-day Nachiyar Koil near Kumbakonam, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified in the early medieval Tevaram poems.
